subject: Customer confirmation: privacy & data integrity checks after incident
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: brief outage investigation - data integrity checks

Marissa,

Quick update from the infra side: yesterday's runtime spike caused a brief metadata-store leader election between 02:14–02:18 UTC. No process crashed, but we saw a small window of elevated latencies and a couple of request retries that triggered additional control-plane logging.

I ran targeted checks this morning across the following systems:
- Object storage access logs (S3 API logs) for read/write anomalies
- Serving runtime audit trail (tokenized request IDs) for duplicated or dropped write operations
- Postgres transaction logs for any rollback/failed commits during the window
- KV cache integrity hashes and prefix checks

Initial findings:
- No write operations were reported as failed or missing in the DB. Transaction commit counts match expected sequence numbers.
- S3 access logs show no unexpected data egress patterns or API keys used outside our fleet IP ranges.
- KV cache had a transient stale prefix but recovered via our background reconciliation; no persisted data loss.

I will consolidate query output into a tailorable summary and hand it to Priyom for customer-facing language. If Neha or Grace want additional checks (e.g., deeper HSM/KMS audit or packet capture review), flag them now.

Rishi
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Customer confirmation: privacy & data integrity checks after incident

Anna,

Thanks again for your patience while we completed our internal review following the service disruption on 2026-03-18 UTC. We understand how important data integrity and privacy are for Acme Corp, so I wanted to share our findings and the checks we ran.

Summary (executive):
- Scope: The event affected a small portion of control-plane requests serviced by a metadata leader election between 02:14–02:18 UTC.
- Impact: We found no evidence of customer data loss or unauthorized data exfiltration.
- Validation steps: review of object-store access logs, database transaction logs, serving runtime audit trail, KV cache integrity hashes, and KMS access records.

Technical details (high level):
- S3 access and object-store logs: No anomalous GET/PUT patterns or egress to unrecognized IP ranges.
- Database (Postgres) transactions: All commits during the window completed or were retried successfully; there are no missing rows for write-heavy customers in our spot checks.
- Serving runtime audit trail: Tokenized request IDs were reconciled — no duplicated final-write markers observed.
- KV cache: A transient stale prefix was detected but reconciled by our background job; no persisted data divergence observed.
- KMS/HSM logs: No external principals accessed keys outside scheduled maintenance windows.

We have attached a short summary of the log queries and results for your security team (log-scan-summary-20260318.pdf) and the raw query extracts (access-audit-queries.txt).

Next steps we recommend:
1) If you want a walk-through of the logs, we can set up a secure screen-share with our infra team and your security contacts.
2) We will add an additional automated post-election audit that runs these reconciliations within 10 minutes of any future leader election.
3) If Acme requires, we can produce an encrypted export of the audit queries and results for your records under your retention policy.

Please let me know if you'd like that call; Priyom is copied to coordinate timing.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: log-scan-summary-20260318.pdf (PDF, 87 KB)
Attachment: access-audit-queries.txt (text, 12 KB)
From: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer confirmation: privacy & data integrity checks after incident

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick and thorough summary. A couple of follow-ups from our security team:
- Can you provide a concise incident timeline (timestamps in UTC) with the detection and reconciliation steps?
- Are the audit results signed or verifiable in a way we can ingest into our compliance system?
- We may need the raw S3 access log excerpts for the window under our retention policies.

If possible, we'd like to schedule a 30-minute call today with Rishi and Priyom to go over the queries; 15:30 UTC would work on our side.

Thanks,
Anna Jensen
Security Operations Lead
Acme Corp
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer confirmation: privacy & data integrity checks after incident

Anna,

Thanks — attaching a concise CSV timeline and the JIRA ticket reference for the internal investigation (JIRA-INC-4521). The timeline includes detection, mitigation, and verification timestamps (all UTC).

We can also provide signed artifacts for the audit outputs. We use our internal signing process (SHA256 with a time-stamped signature) and can produce a PGP-signed bundle upon request; we will place the bundle in a shared, access-controlled Drive folder and share the link to your security mailbox only.

Regarding raw S3 excerpts: we can export the relevant access-log objects for your retention window and provide them in an encrypted tarball. Please confirm the email to send an encrypted access link to, and we'll encrypt with your public key if you have one on file.

I've attached the timeline CSV: timeline-incident-20260318.csv

Priyom Das
Technical Account Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: timeline-incident-20260318.csv (CSV, 3 KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Jensen <anna.jensen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Customer confirmation: privacy & data integrity checks after incident

Anna —

15:30 UTC works for our team. I'll send a calendar invite shortly to lock in the time and include a secure call link. Priyom and Rishi will walk through the timeline and the signed audit bundle; Neha will be on the call for any KMS/HSM questions.

One more confirmation for the record: after exhaustive log checks and transaction reconciliations, Redwood's team has no evidence of data loss or unauthorized exfiltration related to this event. We are treating this as a contained control-plane instability with no customer-data exposure.

We appreciate you escalating this promptly; we'll follow up with the signed bundle and the Drive link immediately after the call.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
